source: The Herald Typhoid cholera re-emerge in Hatcliffe and Epworth (23 March 2017)
processing_notes: Source states: 'An outbreak of cholera has been reported at Rupangwana Clinic in Chiredzi District of Masvingo Province on March 10, 2017 and at Chinyamukwakwa Clinic in Chipinge District of Manicaland Province on March 14, 2017. To date there is one confirmed case at Rupangwana and three suspected in Chinyamukwakwa Clinic of which two have died. The three suspected cases had contact with the confirmed index case admitted at Rupangwana Clinic in Chiredzi District who had come from the border area of Chipinge on March 9, 2017.' - interpreted as 3 sCh cases, 2 deaths. Interpreted as 3 sCh cases and 2 deaths at Chinyamukwakwa Clinic, Chipinge District (Mabee area, flooded, adjacent to the Mozambique border), reported 14 Mar 2017; period from the index case's arrival from the Chipinge border area (9 Mar 2017) to the Minister's statement (article 22/23 Mar 2017). CFR 67% on 3 cases (small numbers; flood-isolated border community). Parts-vs-whole: Chipinge 3 <= JHU Manicaland 2017 provincial total 4 and national 2017 total 6 (3 deaths) - consistent. Provincial subset - do not sum with national row (AI row 504 national Q1 2017 6 cases/3 deaths; AI row 23 and JHU 2017 national rows). District subset - do not sum with the JHU AFR::ZWE::Manicaland 2017 provincial rows (4 cases). [AGENT 2 REVISION 2026-10-04] CONFLICT (Agent 2): The Manica Post ~24 Mar 2017 'Chipinge cholera fears allayed' (https://web.archive.org/web/20170324050706/http://manicapost.co.zw/chipinge-cholera-fears-allayed/), Chipinge District Medical Director Dr Brian Makumbe: 'three suspected cholera cases were detected at Mabee area in Chipinge South. All the three cases tested negative when they were tested at Chipinge District Hospital. The samples were further tested in Harare and were also reported to be negative. Unfortunately two of the three patients died, but they succumbed to diarrehoa' and 'So far we have one case of cholera which was recorded at Rupangwana Clinic in Chiredzi District' (= row 1662). On this account the 3 suspected cases and 2 deaths here were discarded as non-cholera; confidence lowered to 0.25 pending Agent 5 adjudication (retain only if a later MoHCC report re-classifies them). (reason: Agent 2: laboratory-negative per district medical director)
